title: Build Own App or Join a Marketplace? 3 Paths Compared (2026)
description: Should an Indian educator build their own coaching app or teach on a marketplace? Three paths compared on cost, ownership and reach, and when a marketplace alone is enough.
og_description: Own academy, marketplace, or both? A fair 2026 guide for Indian educators: what each path costs, who owns the students, and when teaching only on a big platform is the right call.

h1: Is It Better to Build Your Own App or Join a Marketplace? A 2026 Guide for Indian Educators
dek: Three paths compared fairly: build your own academy and app, teach on a big platform or marketplace, or do both. What each costs, who owns your students, and when a marketplace alone is the right choice.
cover_alt: Build your own app or join a marketplace: three paths for Indian educators compared, own academy, big platforms and marketplaces, checked 24 Oct 2026
audience: Independent educators, tutors and coaching owners in India deciding between their own app and a marketplace
intro: For most independent educators, it is better to build your own academy first, with a website on your own domain and your own Android app (iOS app on Pro or any yearly plan), and to treat marketplaces as extra reach rather than the foundation. Your own academy keeps your brand, your prices and your student list with you. A marketplace or big platform can bring students you would not find alone, but on its terms. Teaching only on a big platform is still the right call for some educators, and this guide says when.

In 2026, "build your own app" no longer means hiring developers. Academy platforms let you set up a website and a branded app yourself, the way Shopify lets a seller open a store without writing code. That changes the old build-or-join trade-off, because building is now a few days of setup, not a lakh-rupee project.

We are AllCoaching, an academy platform that also lists courses on its own marketplace app, so read this knowing who wrote it. Every competitor figure below comes from that company's own website, with the link and the date we checked it.
takeaways: Your own academy means your brand, your prices and your student list, on a website at your domain and an app in your name.
A marketplace or big platform brings reach, but it sets the terms: how you are paid, how courses are priced and who owns the student relationship.

Big Indian edtech brands mostly hire or partner with teachers; Vedantu, for example, publishes its own earnings claim of "₹25,000+ per month @ 4h/day upto ₹75,000+ per month for full time" (checked 24 Oct 2026).
Udemy's instructor revenue share could not be checked on its official page on 24 Oct 2026, so we do not quote a percentage.

Building no longer needs developers: AllCoaching has 0% commission on every monthly plan (from ₹3,999 a month), or yearly Starter at ₹6,999 a year plus a 10% fee on sales, with your own domain and Android app (iOS app on Pro or any yearly plan) on every plan; 7-day free trial, no card.
A marketplace alone suits you if you are new, have no audience yet and want to test demand before building anything.
You can do both: run your own academy and still be discovered on a marketplace; on AllCoaching, your courses can also appear on the AllCoaching app.

sections.h2: How we compared building your own app and joining a marketplace
sections.html:
We compared three paths an Indian educator can take in 2026, using six questions that decide how your teaching business grows.

  1. Who owns the brand students remember: yours or the platform's.
  2. Who holds the student list and whether you can contact students directly.
  3. Who sets the course price and any discounts.
  4. What you pay before you earn, from each company's own pricing page.
  5. Who brings new students: you, the platform, or both.
  6. What happens if you leave: do your students and content come with you?
Disclosure: AllCoaching publishes this guide. We sell an academy platform and also run a marketplace app, so we have a view on this question. Competitor figures link to official pages and carry the date we checked them (24 Oct 2026). Where a company does not publish its educator terms, we say so instead of guessing. If you spot an error, write to contact@allcoaching.in and we will correct it.

sections.h2: The three paths, explained in plain words
sections.html:
There are three real choices, not two: build your own academy, teach on someone else's platform, or build your own and also list on a marketplace.

Path 1: Build your own academy and app

You get a website on your own domain, such as youracademy.in, and an Android and iOS app in your name. Students buy from you, and your student list is yours. You can do this in two ways: hire an agency or app builder to set it up for you, or set it up yourself on an academy platform.

The catch is that students do not arrive on their own. You bring them from YouTube, Instagram, WhatsApp, Telegram, Google search or your offline batches.

Path 2: Join a marketplace or teach for a big platform

Here you teach inside someone else's brand. On a course marketplace such as Udemy, you publish a course to an existing learner base. With Indian edtech brands such as Vedantu, Testbook, Physics Wallah or Unacademy, you usually apply to teach for them, and they handle marketing and technology.

The benefit is reach without marketing. The cost is control: the platform sets the terms, the price and the brand students remember.

{{q:If a marketplace brings students, why build my own academy at all?|Because the students belong to the platform's brand, not yours. If the platform changes its terms or its ranking, your income changes with it. Your own academy is the one place where the student relationship, the price and the brand stay with you.}}

Path 3: Your own academy, plus marketplace discovery

This is the Shopify model applied to coaching. Your academy is your home: your domain, your app, your prices. A marketplace listing is one more doorway into it. On AllCoaching, your courses can also be discovered on the AllCoaching app, while your own website and app stay the main place you sell.

{{fig:before-after|Before and after: an educator split across a big platform, WhatsApp groups, Google Drive notes and UPI screenshots, compared with one academy login with own website, own app, live classes, checkout and marketplace discovery|Whichever path you choose, your students should have one place that is clearly yours.}}

2. An app built for you (agency or app builder)

Good at
A branded website and app set up for you. AppX, for example, says "Launch your own branded app and website for your courses and community. No code needed" and that delivery takes "3-5 days". Classplus says "Get your own brand's teaching app, create your own website & sell courses".
Published price
AppX: not listed on its website (checked 24 Oct 2026); it offers a free personalised demo.[1] Classplus: ₹29,999 for 1 year and ₹39,999 for 2 years; GST, fee on sales and renewal price not stated.[2]
Check
The yearly cost, any fee on sales, under whose developer account the app is published, and who can change the app after launch.
Best for
Owners who prefer a done-for-you setup and are comfortable with a sales process.

3. Teach for a big Indian platform

Good at
Reach and a ready brand. Vedantu calls itself "the top choice for LIVE online classes for K1 to K12". Testbook's partner-faculty page says Testbook handles "marketing, promotions & technology".
Published terms
Vedantu's teacher page states "Earning Potential from minimum ₹ 25,000+ per month @ 4h/day upto ₹ 75,000+ per month for full time" and asks for at least 3 hours of daily availability between 4 and 10 PM; these are Vedantu's own claims.[3] Testbook does not publish pay or revenue share.[4] Physics Wallah hires faculty through its careers page, and Unacademy has no educator terms page we could find (checked 24 Oct 2026).
Check
Ask whether the agreement allows you to run your own academy at the same time, and who owns the recordings you make.
Best for
Teachers who want income without marketing and are happy to teach under another brand.

4. A global course marketplace (Udemy)

Good at
A global course marketplace where instructors publish courses to Udemy's existing learner base.
Published terms
Publishing is not a paid plan; the instructor revenue share is set by Udemy's terms. Its official revenue-share page could not be retrieved on 24 Oct 2026, so we do not quote a percentage here.[5]
Check
The current revenue share on Udemy's own support page, how course prices and discounts are set, and what student details you receive.
Best for
Skill educators (coding, design, spoken English) testing a topic with a global audience.

sections.html:

The honest reading: on published prices, your own academy on AllCoaching costs less up to about ₹2.3 lakh of sales a year. Above that, Classplus's flat listed price is lower on paper, before any fees it may charge. Teaching for a big platform costs nothing upfront, but you also do not set the price or keep the brand, so the comparison is about control more than rupees. On an AllCoaching monthly plan you pay 0% commission, so your cost stays the same as sales rise; above about ₹4 lakh of sales a year that usually costs less than a yearly plan's fee.

Custom apps built by a development agency can cost far more; our guide to white-label coaching app development cost explains what goes into that bill.

sections.h2: When a marketplace alone is the right choice
sections.html:
A marketplace or big platform on its own is the right choice when you want to teach and earn without building an audience, at least for now. That is a sensible decision, not a failure.

  • You are new to teaching online and want to learn how students respond before investing time in your own academy.
  • You have no audience yet on YouTube, Instagram or WhatsApp, and do not want to do marketing.
  • You want predictable hours and income, for example teaching evening classes for a platform while keeping a school job.
  • You are testing a topic, such as a short Excel or spoken English course, with a wide audience.

The time to start your own academy is when students begin to ask for you by name, when you have a few hundred followers who trust you, or when the platform's terms start to limit how you teach or price.

When an agency-built custom app is the right choice

A fully custom app makes sense for a large institute with a real budget, a tech person on staff and features no platform offers. For everyone else, setting up your own academy on a platform gives you the same brand ownership in days, and you can change it yourself.

YouTube or Instagram educator with an audience

Build your own academy. Your followers already know your name, so send them to your own website and app instead of someone else's. Our guide on monetising a YouTube teaching channel through your own app shows how.

Offline coaching institute moving online

Build your own academy so current students, parents and new admissions see your institute's name. See how to move offline coaching online.

New teacher with no audience

Start on a platform or marketplace, learn what students want, and build your own academy once you have demand. Our guide to getting your first 500 students helps when you are ready.

Exam educator worried that a new app will not get downloads

Give students a website first and the app as an option, and use marketplace discovery as an extra doorway. Read why a coaching app may not be getting students before you build.

sections.h2: How to start your own academy without leaving a marketplace
sections.html:
You do not have to choose on day one. Build your own academy alongside the platform you teach on now, and move your audience across at your own pace.

{{fig:switch|Four steps to start your own academy while still teaching on a marketplace: build your academy, keep teaching where you are, bring your own audience home, add marketplace discovery|Your own academy grows while your current income continues.}} {{steps}}

We built AllCoaching because we kept seeing the same split: educators had to pick between owning their brand and being found. In our experience, the educators who do best treat the marketplace as a shop window and their own academy as the shop. If you later move fully from one platform to another, follow our checklist on switching coaching apps without losing students.

items: Start the 7-day trial, connect your domain and upload one complete course with a free demo lesson.
Continue on your current platform; ask whether your agreement allows you to run your own academy too.
Put your academy and app link in YouTube descriptions, Instagram bio and WhatsApp groups.
Let your courses also appear on the AllCoaching app, so new students can find you there.

faq: Is it better to build your own app or join a marketplace?

For most independent educators, build your own academy first and use marketplaces as extra reach. Your own website and app keep your brand, prices and student list with you, while a marketplace brings students on its terms. If you are new and have no audience, starting on a marketplace is reasonable.
How much does it cost to build your own coaching app in India?

On an academy platform, much less than a custom build. AllCoaching takes 0% commission on every monthly plan from ₹3,999 a month, or yearly from ₹6,999 plus a 10% fee on sales, with your own domain and Android app (iOS app on Pro or any yearly plan) on every plan. Classplus lists ₹29,999 for one year. AppX does not list prices. A custom agency build costs more and varies by scope.
What is wrong with only teaching on a marketplace like Udemy or Unacademy?

Nothing, if you are comfortable with the platform setting the terms. The limits are that students remember the platform's brand, pricing is not fully yours, and your income depends on its rules and ranking. Udemy's revenue share could not be checked on its official page on 24 Oct 2026.
When is joining a marketplace alone the right choice?

When you are new, have no audience, do not want to do marketing, or want to test a topic before building anything. Many educators start this way and build their own academy once students ask for them by name.
Can I have my own app and still be on a marketplace?

Yes. On AllCoaching, your academy has its own website and Android app (iOS app on Pro or any yearly plan), and your courses can also be discovered on the AllCoaching marketplace app. If you teach for another platform, check whether your agreement allows it.
Will I lose brand control on a platform that also has a marketplace?
Not if your academy runs on your own domain and app. On AllCoaching, students who buy through your website or app see your brand; the marketplace listing is an extra way to be found.
How much do teachers earn on platforms like Vedantu?

Vedantu's own teacher page states earning potential from ₹25,000+ per month at 4 hours a day up to ₹75,000+ per month full time. These are Vedantu's claims, checked 24 Oct 2026, not a published revenue share.
Do I need an app at all to teach online?

Not on day one. A website on your own domain with UPI checkout is enough to start selling. An app helps with repeat learning and notifications once students are enrolled, and on AllCoaching it comes with every plan.
